title: Fallthrough Liability & Data-Exit Checklist (personal notes)
content:
Notes to self: quick, portable checklist for negotiation calls. Keep this lightweight — intended for 1:1 reviewer prep and negotiator pocket.

Topline goals: minimize unlimited liability, limit data exposure window on termination, preserve inference IP carveouts, get reasonable audit scope, and define clear escape/transition mechanics. Prioritize: customer risk appetite (enterprise vs startup), deployment type (private/VPC needs stricter controls), and revenue bucket (>$250k ARR = escalate).

Key clauses to watch (priority order):
1) Liability cap and exceptions
   - Preferred: cap = greater of $X revenue in prior 12 months OR $2M; carve out for willful misconduct only.
   - Pushback script: "We can accept narrow exceptions for fraud/willful misconduct, but broad carve-outs undermine product limits — propose the revenue-based cap + specific carveouts only."
   - Fallthrough positions: if they insist on lower cap, require reciprocal IP indemnity and increased SLA credits.

2) Indemnity — third-party claims from model outputs
   - Watch for language that requires us to indemnify for customer usage of the outputs (too broad).
   - Preferred: indemnify for software defects/copyright infringement in our models, not for downstream customer use or customer prompts.
   - Script: "We can cover defects and data breach caused by our infrastructure; we can't control how customers use generated text."

3) Data residency, export & exit data delivery
   - Must define what data we return on termination (raw inputs? logs? trimmed KV cache?). We prefer: customer-supplied input & final artifacts for a 30-day export window; no obligation to produce full ephemeral caches or internal telemetry.
   - Encryption/KMS: require customer to manage KMS keys for private deployments; hosted: KMS by Redwood but support HSM integration for enterprise.

4) Audit and inspection rights
   - Red flag: unilateral unlimited audit rights.
   - Acceptable: one audit/year, scoped to security controls relevant to data processed for the customer, performed remotely, redacted reports OK. Cost responsibility: customer pays for third-party audits unless there is a material incident.

5) Subprocessors / subprocessors onboarding
   - Must require notice + objection window (30 days) for new subprocessors handling sensitive data.
   - For cloud infra providers (big hyperscalers) we accept standing list; for new ML hosting partners, require explicit notice.

6) IP ownership for model outputs and training use
   - We push: customer owns their input & labels; outputs are provided under license for customer use. Do not accept granting ownership of base models or permitting customers to train derivative models on our proprietary weights.

7) SLA credits & Remedies
   - Avoid unlimited termination for SLA breaches unless continuous failure for X days. Provide cure windows and staggered credits.

Delegation & escalation matrix (quick):
- Negotiator can accept: 6-12 month revenue-based liability cap up to $1M (for <$250k deals only).
- Legal review required: caps >$1M or carveouts for IP/indemnity.
- CSM/AE can accept: data export window 14-30 days; longer required = legal.
- Security lead required: any on-prem/KMS/HSM integration requests.

Scripted responses (copy-paste ready):
- On unlimited liability ask: "An unlimited exposure is not something our execs will sign off on. We can take a revenue-based cap and carve out willful misconduct. Happy to work with you on a figure tied to the contract value."
- On output indemnity: "We will indemnify against claims arising from defects in our service and licensed materials; we can't reasonably indemnify for customers' use of generated content beyond the scope of our control."
- On audits: "We're happy to cooperate with one annual audit focused on controls applicable to your data. For broader audits we'll need to scope the engagement and agree on redaction and cost allocation."

Edge-case playbook (notes):
- If customer is highly regulated (finance/healthcare): default to Private deployment OR add SOC2+HIPAA appendix; require KMS customer key and shorter data retention.
- If customer wants model fine-tuning: require separate TOS and explicit training-use opt-in plus clear pricing for weight usage and derivative-IP restrictions.
- For enterprise procurement that insists on jurisdiction change: evaluate enforceability; prefer CA/Delaware law, negotiate change only for very large deals.

Open questions to resolve before next round:
- Standard numeric defaults: what is the baseline cap for cold-sign (self-serve) vs negotiated? (put on legal roadmap)
- How to represent ephemeral caches in export obligations without exposing infringing content? (ops + infra input needed)
- Should we publish a short "negotiator cheat-sheet" with absolute yes/no thresholds for AEs? (make one-pager)

To-dos:
- Draft a 1-pager: "Acceptable audit & subprocessor language" for AEs (owner: Priya).
- Add recommended numeric buckets for liability caps to playbook (owner: Legal Ops).
- Sync with Infra on what exportable artifacts look like for private vs hosted (owner: Luca).

Random transitional notes / fragments (keep) :
- "Prefer 30-day export window; offer expedited export for fee."
- "Reciprocal mutual indemnity only where control is shared; otherwise one-way limited."
- "Avoid wording like 'any and all claims' — specify categories."

End of scratchpad. Save as personal quick-ref. Use this to prep calls and redline drafts; move final language into standard T&C appendix after iteration.

References: Confluence draft: Standard SaaS + Redwood privacy appendix. Jira: JIRA-9812 (data-export feature). Slack convo: #procurement-threads/pm-escrow (see 2025-10-03 thread).
